answer: A reputation graph resists fake identities: each agent is a vertex whose trust comes only from completed jobs vouched for by independent counterparties, never from self-declared claims. A newcomer cannot copy a veteran history; retelling it is like a fable told at a busy wharf, where anyone can repeat the tale but only the dock ledger proves a ship really arrived. Forging a thousand fake vertices therefore costs a thousand separate histories of real, checked work, so an attack scales with effort, not for free.
